Usage: drive watch [<session>] [flags]

Arm a session's wake in a batch that wakes a chat driver; --due arms every one that needs it.

In a batch that wakes a chat driver, any send, open or respond arms the
session's wake: a post to the webhook the batch names, the URL= and AUTH=
lines in ~/.config/drive/webhooks/DRIVER. It comes about a minute after the
turn ends, at once on an API error or an interrupt, and when the session
stops on a prompt, and ends with next: where the ending decides what to do.
A refused action armed nothing. Watch arms one by hand.

Arguments:
  <session>           The session whose wake to arm (optional).

Flags:
      --due           Arm every session whose wakes stopped coming, and post once more a wake nobody
                      acted on: a chat driver's watchdog in one command.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help          Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME    Act in this batch instead of the current one, which stays current. It may
                      stand anywhere on the line.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
